correctness.rationale: Independent exact subset dynamic programming assigns weight −1 to a selected support edge and +1 to every other edge, sums paths starting at 0 through each visited set with each final vertex, and appends the closing edge. Each undirected Hamiltonian incidence set is counted twice, with the same sign, so halving gives exactly the specified Walsh sum. The empty support gives 1344 cycles, and edge transitivity gives 672 using each edge, so all singleton coefficients vanish. Each automorphism fixing 0 is determined by its permutation of the four neighbors, since distances to 0 and those neighbors determine any vertex. Translations and coordinate permutations thus give all 384 automorphisms. Representative DP values expanded over the 6 pair and 24 triple orbits reproduce both full histograms, zero pair coefficients at no supports, and 1120 zero triples in six orbits of sizes 64, 96, 192, 192, 192, 384. The six listed representatives were checked against this partition. Each vertex cut meets any cycle evenly. A cut taking a singleton to a triple has size at most four. The exhaustive cut check finds only the 16 stars at these sizes. Independently, for a smaller shore of size k≤8 the induced edge bound e≤k log₂(k)/2 follows by splitting on a bit and using binary entropy H(p)≥2p when p≤1/2. Thus for 2≤k≤8 the cut has size at least k(4−log₂(k))≥6 by concavity; the k=1 shores are precisely the stars. These give 64 distinct singleton-derived zeros, leaving 1056 non-cut-derived triples in the stated sense.
residual_risks: The theorem does not classify frequencies of weight at least four or all equivalences under arbitrary functions constant on the cycle ensemble; the forced-cancellation comparison is about cuts from singleton supports.

evidence: For a support S the Walsh sum is Σ_{A⊆S}(−2)^|A| N(A), where N(A) counts cycles containing A. Thus exact marked-edge joint inclusion counts would be an equivalent route to the audit, as would the signed edge weighting used in the replay.

The inspected prescribed-edge sources and summaries concern whether N(A) is positive, not the complete collection of its counts. The local signed-dimer census uses 272 perfect matchings, not connected unions of two of them.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Existence cannot determine equality between the positive and negative terms of the signed count. Dimer marginals alone do not evaluate the connectedness-filtered matching-pair problem; the Hamiltonicity filter requires joint data.

value.rationale: Hamiltonian cycles in the four-cube are a natural structured discrete ensemble, and low-degree signed incidence moments probe dependencies not visible in the cycle count. The exact absence of quadratic cancellation, the full cubic orbit classification, and the large set of zeros beyond the evident cut mechanism give a meaningful benchmark for low-degree detection and for analogous cube or tour problems. The enumeration is exhaustive in its stated degree range rather than a chosen subset of convenient labels.
residual_risks: No proof of a corresponding pattern in higher dimensions or at larger frequency supports.
